rows.scene: Bhattathiri offers salutations to Guruvayurappan as the source and ground of the cosmos; show the scholar before a serene blue deity with a quiet symbolic universe surrounding them.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v010; producer pass. Krishna face/chest/palms B-R 114/108 and 99/113; Bhattathiri face/shoulder/arm R-B 96/99/102. Both open hands show five separated digits and both feet five toes; no enclosing oval. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Bhattathiri offered his salutations to Lord Guruvayoorappan, who is responsible for creation and protection of this universe, who is in the form of the universe, whose radiance gives brightness for this universe, whose description is beyond words and comprehension, whose true nature cannot be understood by even Devas and divine sages.

rows.scene: Bhattathiri salutes the formless Brahman who assumes many forms through maya while remaining complete; render one central Vishnu form reflected in a quiet field of differentiated worlds.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v007; producer pass. Krishna face/torso/palms B-R 97/86 and 88/84; Bhattathiri face/back/arm R-B 89/88/92. Both open deity hands show five separated digits; feet show five toes. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Bhattathiri prostrated to that Brahman who is beyond the birth and death cycle, who is beyond good and bad deeds, who is above three Gunas,, accepted the Maaya, exhibited knowledge-ignorance, wealth and though formless took up various forms to protect the people of the world, while remaining in state of Supreme bliss.

rows.scene: A non-figurative contemplation of Brahman beyond every named category, centered on a calm unoccupied field of warm cream and deep indigo with earthly forms receding at its edges.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v006; producer pass. No deity. Four skin-only figure patches R-B 90, 95, 98, 91. Three celestial figures, two people and three asuras remain distinct; no digit counts applicable at this scale. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: The Parabrahman form is neither a bird, nor an animal, human, deva, asura, female, male, not even five elements of nature, good or bad deeds, not three Gunas, living or non-living. If there is some thing left behind all these, then that form which even hundreds of vedas find it difficult to explain is the supreme Brahman.

rows.scene: Brahman appears through maya as creator and withdraws creation like a tortoise drawing in its limbs; portray the world gathered inward around a calm Vishnu form as darkness settles.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v006; producer pass. Guruvayurappan face/torso B-R 47/46; Bhattathiri R-B 114/109; Brahma torso R-B 119. Brahma has four contracted heads and four attached arms; no extra figures or limbs observed. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Bhattathiri offered his salutations to the Brahman who reflects HIMSELF in HIS Maaya and created the whole universe using the Mahat, Ahankara, five senses Panchabhootas. During pralaya, the entire creation is destroyed and pulled back to the supreme Brahman form just like how the tortoise pulls its body inside its shell, causing an intense darkness everywhere, yet the supreme Brahman shines unaffected by the darkness.

rows.scene: Bhattathiri praises Krishna as sound, action, atom and time, the one cause of the universe; show him in a serene compact cosmic tableau with subtle symbols of sound, matter and time.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v005; producer pass. Krishna face/arm/palms B-R 74/74 and 78/51; Bhattathiri face/shoulder/arm R-B 117/115/116. Both open deity hands show five separated digits and feet show five toes. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Bhattathiri offered his salutations to Bhagwan Krishna, who is mentioned as primeval sound, actions, atom, time, whose supreme form is explained in Vedas as Purusha, Supreme consciousness, atma, who has the ability to create the maaya just from the corner of his eye.

rows.scene: The rope mistaken for a snake conveys avidya; show Bhattathiri in a dim forest noticing a worn rope clearly as knowledge dawns, with a symbolic grove suggesting samsara.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v005; producer pass. No deity. Bhattathiri face/shoulder/forearm R-B 80/80/78; folded hands partly tucked and feet covered. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: It is difficult to explain Bhagwan’s swaroopam as to whether it exists or does not exists due to ignorance, just like it is difficult to differentiate between a rope and a snake in darkness. By singing the praises of Bhagwan and practising those mentioned in scriptures, one can gain the knowledge to cut the dark forest of Samsara.

rows.scene: Gold ornaments and clay pots share their underlying substance, while waking reveals the dream and clear seeing resolves the rope; compose these three analogies as one balanced mural around Bhattathiri.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v004; producer pass. No deity. Bhattathiri cheek/chest/upper-arm R-B 99/112/117; folded hands are visible and feet fully covered. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Just as jewels are made of gold, pots are made of mud & just as for a dreamer, on waking up, darkness vanishes, a worn out rope is seen clearly. Similarly one understands the divine form only after gaining the divine knowledge. Bhattathiri offered salutations to that form of Bhagwan

rows.candidate_status: Selected v010; producer pass. Krishna face/chest/palms B-R 90/89 and 79/83; Bhattathiri face/arm R-B 96/104, two devas 105/103, Brahma 102. rows.commentary: Bhattathiri prostrated to Bhagwan Krishna, from whom the sun, fire, wind, brahma, devas originated, learnt to do their work as purpose of the creation and loose their positions after the purpose is over and who created and control this entire universe.

rows.scene: Bhattathiri prays to one central Krishna, whose unity holds the many threes together; use three balanced arcs and restrained nonverbal triadic cues around the single deity and scholar.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v004; producer pass after exact-image reinspection. Guruvayurappan face/forearm B-R 73/89; Bhattathiri face/arm R-B 86/107. Both deity hands show five digits; both feet five toes. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Bhattathiri prayed to Bhagwan Krishna through the creator of the 3 Gunas, one who is the meaning of the 3 letter word ''Pranava'', one who is the manifestation of  the Trinity, whose true nature is described by 3 vedas, who is the pure consciousness and exists in all the 3 states - awakening, sleeping, dreaming, one who has measured this entire universe in just HIS 3  strides, who remains unchanged in past, present and future times, who is worshipped by the means of 3 yogas - Gyaan, Bhakti and Karma.

rows.scene: The eternal, pure and changeless form shines within the hearts of unattached sages; show one serene Krishna presence reflected in the inward contemplation of a small group of distinct sages.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v003; producer pass. Guruvayurappan face/forearm B-R 54/68. All three sages' sampled face/arm patches R-B 54/76, 59/68 and 69/67; hands rest on thighs, feet covered. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Bhagwan’s form is eternal, pure, ever awake, devoid of bondages and actions, transcends all dualities, changeless, the originating point of forgiveness, truth, mercy, wealth and all good qualities, causeless, perfect and exhibiting limitless glory, exists in non-attachment hearts, shines with supreme consciousness.

rows.scene: Bhattathiri seeks refuge at Vishnu’s feet from the irresistible wheel of time; show a great twelve-spoked wheel held at a respectful distance while the scholar bows at the deity’s lotus feet.
rows.candidate_status: Selected v006; producer pass. Krishna face/forearm/palms B-R 98/42 and 104/102; Bhattathiri face/shoulder/forearm R-B 98/110/97. Both open hands show five digits, both feet five toes, and time wheel has twelve spokes. Independent exact-checksum review pending; artwork unapproved.
rows.commentary: Bhagwan’s wheel of time with its twelve spokes (months), and 360 teeth (days) is irreversible, going round with very high speed, capable of destroying the world in a minute. Having surrendered at the lotus feet of Bhagwan Krishna, Bhattathiri pleaded protection from the woes caused by the time wheel and from all afflictions.
